about: Headless bot playtests of Lure v5, the flight (game/pods/bots), 15 runs per cell on the final tuning. Bots are skill proxies, not taste proxies. 'random' = no-skill floor; 'evader' = crude competent player: flees and swirls, dodges telegraphs, keeps off rocks and mines, cruises left of centre. A full run is 6 sectors x 40s = 240s. arena = mean sector reached (of 6).
tuning_history: First pass: evader averaged sector 2.3-2.5 and the random bot hit rocks within ~6s. Sectors 1-2 softened (fewer rocks and chasers) so sector 1 onboards rather than walls.

Found and fixed a telemetry bug: in a continuous flow the next sector starts inside the 'arenaCleared' handler, so 'escaped' was recorded on the wrong sector. Now arenaExit carries {cleared}. 0 inconsistent runs after the fix.
notes: The bot never wins (0/30), but it's the crudest proxy yet: it can't plan a path through a scrolling field. Mikael has out-performed the evader in every version (v4: critic expected arena 2, he reached 6 and won twice). Expect him to get much further.
Runs now last minutes (P9): bot runs up to 207s, a full flight is 240s.
A vs B (scroll speed 95 vs 140 px/s) are matched in difficulty for the bot (2.53 vs 2.93 sectors).
